the 31 place-years of buildings and dress: this run's camera pass walks them now (about five minutes; the pilot walks a loop through each stop so the frames catch the world mid-stride, and each stop also reads the wheat price, credit terms and ruler systems there). Verdict becomes PASS or FAIL when the folder arrives and the frames are judged against the packs

this exact view and the sky day and night at the current year: the camera pass shoots them first (etest_now_*.png, etest_sky_day.png, etest_sky_night.png; the clock is put back). For any other century: set the date and run the test again
accents, wrapping and GUI scale: the camera pass ends by photographing a test book page (etest_book_accents.png); the frame settles Findings 11 and 30

the run measures its own smoothness instead of asking: every shot's fps and client tick ms land in etest_perf.txt beside the frames, and every era-stop line carries server tick ms; only how it looks in motion to a human is left, and that is the folder's judgement

true multiplayer (a second human): the run exercises talk and trade with NPCs as the counterparty, and one player's session can be photographed; a real second player is the one thing no in-run alternative can fake
hours of play feel: the day-pass borrows one full day round and gives it back (see day-pass in the living phase); what is left is the feel of many real hours, which no compression can honestly fake
